free_tier.stated: 'Segfault offers free unlimited Root Servers. A new server (inside a Virtual Machine) is created for every SSH connection.' Access is an ssh login as root on segfault.net with the password 'segfault'; no signup, no email, no account. The free server carries restrictions: 'The storage, memory, processing power and bandwidth is limited.'

per_object_cap.stated: one root server per SECRET; a new SECRET yields a new server with a new /sec filesystem. Not a cap on how many you may hold.

retention.stated: 'Data in your home directory and in /sec, /onion and /everyone are permanent. This data is cleared only if the server is not logged in for 30+ days.' Root filesystem and /tmp are wiped at logout: 'Data in (/usr, /tmp, ...) is only valid for the duration of the session'.

egress.terms: 'the outbound traffic is throttled' on the free service; the throttle rate is not published. Outbound is routed through Mullvad/CryptoStorm/NordVPN exit nodes.

interface_detail: SSH only, on port 22 or 443, plus a `.onion` and `.gsocket` route. Root inside the guest. No web console, no API. A reverse TCP/UDP port on a public IP is provided; `curl sf/port` prints the IP and port.
tooling: any SSH client; OpenSSH must be new enough to support `-o SetEnv` (the FAQ names 'Bad configuration option: setenv' as the failure on old clients)
chaining: An anonymous root shell with a public reverse port and no account of any kind: the cheapest possible way to hold a WireGuard endpoint or a cron-driven monitor without giving up an identity, at the cost of a 1.5-day idle reap.

limits.value: auto-shutdown when no shell is running in tmux or screen and nobody has logged in for 1.5 days
permanent data in /sec cleared after 30+ days without a login
free servers are resource-restricted; the numeric memory, CPU and storage caps are not published on any page read
outbound traffic is throttled on the free tier; the rate is not published

binding_note: The free tier's memory, CPU and disk caps are unpublished, so the first thing that fails is whatever the per-container limit is, and you cannot know it before logging in and running `cat /config/self/limits`.

identity_cost.detail: no account, no email, no card, no phone, no document. The login is `ssh [address removed]` with the password 'segfault'; a per-server SECRET is generated at login and is the only thing that identifies the machine back to you. Nothing is registered anywhere.

reliability_note: No reliability event observed. The operator states it may shut free servers down under resource contention and that it is 'no company' run in spare time, which is a capacity statement rather than an observed outage.
confidence_note: The machine's numeric shape is unverified: no first-party page publishes it, and the config file in the public repository has every limit commented out.

notes: The only provider with a genuinely anonymous identity cost: no signup form exists to be filled in. Three things are unresolved and all three need a login must not perform. First, the numeric shape (vCPU, RAM, disk) is not on any first-party page; `cat /config/self/limits` prints it after login. A third-party writeup (nixsanctuary.com) states 128 MB personal storage, 16 GB shared and a read-only rootfs at 500 Mbit/s, which is reported-only and contradicts nothing but is unconfirmed. Second, the outbound throttle rate is unpublished. Third, 'unlimited Root Servers' is the operator's phrase; whether it means unbounded concurrent servers is unstated. The guest has no systemd, so a daemon has to be started from /sec/usr/etc/rc.local. A reverse port is explicitly provided, so an inbound listener works without a static IP of your own.

shape.note: not published on any first-party page; the config file in the public repo has the limits commented out and the FAQ points at `cat /config/self/limits` inside the guest

extras.term: per session; persistent storage survives 30 days of non-use
extras.price_arithmetic: no charge at any point and no payment field exists, so there is no rate to multiply

network_out.ports: one reverse TCP/UDP port on a public IP, assigned by the service; `curl sf/port` prints IP and port

session_cap.note: no wall clock while a shell is attached; auto-shutdown after 1.5 days with no login and no shell in tmux or screen. Every login without the SECRET creates a fresh server.

extras.payment_methods: none; there is no billing system and no account to bill
